question: When 5.3 g of sodium carbonate reacts with 6.0 g of ethanoic acid, the products are 2.2 g of carbon dioxide, 0.9 g of water and a sodium ethanoate residue. Show that these observations agree with conservation of mass.
options: Mass of reactants = 5.3 g + 6.0 g = 11.3 g. Mass of products = 2.2 g (CO2) + 0.9 g (H2O) + 8.2 g (Sodium ethanoate) = 11
explanation: Mass of reactants = 5.3 g + 6.0 g = 11.3 g. Mass of products = 2.2 g (CO2) + 0.9 g (H2O) + 8.2 g (Sodium ethanoate) = 11.3 g. Since Reactant Mass = Product Mass (11.3 g = 11.3 g), conservation of mass is verified.

question: Why must a chemical equation be balanced?
options: According to the Law of Conservation of Mass, atoms are neither created nor destroyed during chemical transformations. T
explanation: According to the Law of Conservation of Mass, atoms are neither created nor destroyed during chemical transformations. Therefore, the total number of atoms of each element on the reactant side must strictly equal the number on the product side.

Example: 2 H2O --Electricity--> 2 H2 + O2.
